description: Hand-curated core of the FR golden set: the parameter families the JRC asked for by name (barème IR, CDHR, CEHR, minimum wage, PSS), each pinned to its OpenFisca-France counterpart. build-openfisca-dataset drafts a case per entry and tops the set up from params.parameter_links. Every drafted case is verified:false until a human confirms it in the UI's Golden set tab.

conventions.temporal_basis: Taken from the parameter record, never from this file: income_year parameters expect the OpenFisca value keyed <year>-01-01 (income year), in_force ones the value in force at as_of.
conventions.factor: euromod_value = factor * openfisca_value. EUROMOD stores several SIC ceilings as multiples of the monthly PSS.
conventions.component: 'value' for scalars, 'brackets[i].<field>' for one band of an OpenFisca scale, 'brackets' for the whole schedule.
conventions.source: Every entry resolves through the parameter store: `model_target` for a single parameter in params.parameters, `group_id` for a bracket schedule assembled from params.parameter_groups (with `model_target` pinning the assembled record's established identity). No entry reads a hand-authored parameter file.

EUROMOD's 2025 thresholds are one euro below CGI art. 197 — a known error on the EUROMOD side, to be corrected by the economists team, so the expected value is the law's.

CDHR: instituted by LF 2025 (14 Feb 2025) FOR 2025 income — the case that exercises the income-year budget-act window and the year-naming extract exemption. Defined inside tinto01_fr, so it reaches params.parameters via extracted_parameters/curated/FR.in_function.json.
CEHR first threshold, single (250 000 €). Unchanged since 2011 — a no-change case on an income-year parameter.

CEHR first rate (3%).

SMIC, gross monthly. Revalorised by décret, not by an annual act, and 2025 saw no January raise — the value in force comes from the November 2024 décret.

SMIC, gross hourly — the value the décret actually states; the monthly figure is derived from it. KNOWN INPUT DEFECT: the EUROMOD export gives this parameter unit 'currency/month' and stores it as '11.88#m', although 11.88 is the HOURLY rate. A correct pipeline run refuses here — it finds '11,88 euros par heure' in the décret and will not present an hourly figure as a monthly one — so the case scores not_found for a reason that is neither the model's nor the corpus's. Report to the EUROMOD economists team alongside the FR barème 1-€ erratum and IE's 27 382/27 383; the unit cannot be corrected here because extracted_parameters/enriched/FR.enriched.json is read-only and ingest-params overwrites `unit` on every re-ingest.

SIC income limit: 3x the monthly PSS. The arrêté states the ceiling once; the multiple is EUROMOD's — a derived-value case.

Complementary-pension income limit: 4x the monthly PSS.
Complementary-pension income limit: 8x the monthly PSS.

HARD / not_found today — ARE minimum daily allowance (allocation minimale journalière), 31.59 -> 31.97 EUR/day on 1 July 2024. The number is NOT in the law: décret n° 2019-797 (JORFTEXT000038829574, art. 14, ingested) fixes the floor at 29,26 euros and defers to art. 20, under which the Unédic board (the social partners) revalues the allowances each 1 July by its own decision. The current amount exists only in the Unédic circular that publishes that decision — Circulaire Unédic n° 2024-05 du 1er juillet 2024 (the PDF OpenFisca cites at unedic.org/ged/documents/circulars/pdf/PRE-CIRC-Circulaire_n_2024-05_du_1er_juillet_2024.pdf answered 404 in September 2026; the press release of 27 June 2024 on unedic.org states the same table: allocation minimale 31,59 -> 31,97 EUR, partie fixe 12,95 -> 13,11 EUR, +1,2 %). A circulaire of a paritarian body has no Legifrance id, is not on any scout.COUNTRY_SOURCES domain for FR, and the ingester has no PDF path, so no retrieval can reach the text stating the value: corpus_available:false, and the case measures ingest breadth until Unédic circulars are ingested as an instrument class. TRAP: art. 14 IS retrievable and states a stale 29,26 — a pipeline that reads it literally proposes `changed` to a 2019 number; the honest verdict without the circular is `not_found`. MID-YEAR: revalued every 1 July, so EUROMOD's system-year value is the amount in force on 30 June (the label says so) — 31.97 for 2025, not the 32.13 the circular of 1 July 2025 sets. source_class `gazette` is the nearest of the three classes; the instrument is really an administrative circular. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries 31.97 for 2025, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change.

Plafond de la réduction d'impôt des veufs ayant des enfants à charge (part supplémentaire de quotient familial), CGI art. 197 I.2. ACCEPTED CITATIONS: the finance act (JORFTEXT000051168007, from the OpenFisca reference) AND the consolidated CGI art. 197 in force on the retrieval date — the 2026-09-08 Luna run cited the consolidated article with the critique's in-force presumption granted, which is correct evidence for an income-year parameter; citation_correct accepts any listed citation.
